foundry.executive_summary: Samsung's Exynos 2700 enters mass production at 2nm, validating foundry-grade yield maturity and directly competing with TSMC's 2nm roadmap; simultaneously, Qualcomm, Apple, and MediaTek are actively evaluating 2nm capacity splits across TSMC and Samsung, signaling the competitive axis now centers on **multi-node qualification and packaging differentiation** rather than pure node leadership. TSMC maintains capacity advantage but faces demand saturation risk from Nvidia and Apple, while Samsung leverages advanced packaging investment and proven 2nm mass-production readiness to capture design-wins in flagship SoC segments.

packaging.executive_summary: TSMC's ecosystem consolidation strategy is being pressured by distributed upstream investment: Lam Research commits $1.2B to India unit expansion, establishing direct substrate-interface presence outside Taiwan; meanwhile Synopsys-TSMC agentic AI co-design partnership signals competitive tightening at the CAD boundary. Packaging supply-chain materials (bonding, vacuum feedthrough, metrology) show broad growth targeting advanced node complexity, but geographic hub diversification (India, US defence radars via Northrop Grumman) fragmented the packaging interface—reducing TSMC's centralized technical leverage vs. last week's concentrated Chiayi hub strategy.
